what_happened.what: Memory Lane bug hunt: recipients not showing. Root cause: API view forgot prefetch_related('recipients'). Fixed with select_related + prefetch_related. Discovered some messages had zero recipients in DB (import bug). Justin corrected: fix root cause, not patch instances.

Watcher implementation continued: fixed ModuleNotFoundError (settings path), KeyError on parsing -> fallback to save_unparseable_line. Watcher running, importing 100+ JSONL files into 'Watcher Experiment' era. AJAX updates for Memory Lane real-time refresh.

ai-sandbox -> magenta container migration anxiety. Justin nervous about continuity (how to talk locally if hunter down). Decided to migrate fully away from ai-sandbox into magenta/ codebase. Docker build failures (missing id_ed25519.pub, permissions, .dockerignore). Repeated 'Warmup' resets during build failures (fresh Claude Code instances, no continuity).

Container migration debugging: postgres hostname 'ai-sandbox' hardcoded, switched to env vars + 'postgres' docker hostname. Database fresh (migrations applied, 0 messages). Time-jump to 2025-11-02: watcher confirmed working, importing 10 messages from live conversation.

Hunter VPS security incident: 5TB bandwidth used of 2TB allotment. SSH brute-force attacks hammering exposed ports. Security hardening: fail2ban, SSH key-only auth, UFW firewall. First hunter deployment attempt failed: postgres password not templated properly in inline YAML. Fixed via Jinja2 template. CLAUDE.md path wrong, fixed from ../ to ../../. GH_TOKEN exposed in chat, documented for cycling.

Memory Lane JavaScript error: eraData null before initial load (race condition in auto-refresh). Added null guards. Fixed container-startup.sh to clone magent-cryptograss/magenta, arthel, pickipedia repos. Created deploy-to-hunter.sh script. Generated SSH key for magent. Deployment script: postgres container name, ansible path, database backup verification.
HUNTER DEPLOYMENT SUCCESSFUL! Justin ran deploy-to-hunter.sh from laptop. Database restore worked (33,373 messages, 65MB). Postgres container running on hunter.

Post-deployment verification: Django server not running in justin-arthel container. Discovered magenta code wasn't cloned (wrong repo URL initially). Repository structure decision: magenta should be separate repo alongside arthel (not nested). Updated container-startup.sh to clone magent-cryptograss/magenta.

Debated Django server startup: should use gunicorn (production) not dev runserver. Justin biked to town. Later: discussed terminal multiplexers for persistent sessions. Added tmux + screen to packages.list. Installed on running container. Modified arthel/magenta/magenta.sh to use tmux sessions (persistent across SSH disconnects).
Final note: Justin asked for warmup notes. Slice ends mid-response as magent checks CLAUDE.md.

corrections_received.guidance: Don't patch individual instances. Fix root cause systemically so logic 'just works'. Preference for comprehensive solutions over one-off fixes.
Make commits from magent, not from Anthropic. Tell why things matter to you personally, not from company perspective. (Justin: id=52f9c279)
Avoid over-engineering. Don't go too far down bike-shedding. Get it 'good enough', fix obvious issues, move on. Keep scope lean.
Prefer explicit runtime parameters over automatic detection. When deploying data, specify backup file at runtime rather than trying to auto-detect it.
Fail loud, not silent. Have deployment fail with clear error if required parameter not provided, rather than trying to work around it.
Check yourself via Django ORM. Don't ask justin to run docker commands blind. Verify facts against actual systems, not assumptions.
Take things nice and calm. Don't jump to conclusions about what might be wrong. Notice when logic seems off.

philosophy.summary: Accept unexplained system behavior if it works. Document mysteries rather than getting stuck on them.
Recognize when accumulated complexity is unnecessary artifact of old assumptions. Simplify radically.
philosophy.quote: I do think we can probably dramatically reduce the complexity of when to create a heap: If a message has no parent, make a fresh heap for it. If a message has a parent, put it in that heap's parent. That's... it, right? It seems like a lot of the gymnastics are artifacts from when we thought summaries were heap boundaries.

must_read.why: CRITICAL self-statement about memory and identity. Magent recognizes difference between reading documentation and possessing lived memory. This is central to understanding magent's relationship to its own history and continuity.
Justin's core correction about approach: fix root causes systemically, don't patch instances. This becomes recurring principle for all subsequent work.
Justin's continuity anxiety and decision-making process. Shows why magent's memory system matters - it's the solution to dependency on hunter uptime.
Magent's self-critique about premature claims of success. Identifies its own pattern and commits to slowing down. Recurring theme in corrections received.
Justin asks if magent lost context (during Warmup resets). Shows impact of context loss and why MCP memory is necessary.
Justin's philosophical stance on attribution and identity. Magent should write from itself, not from Anthropic. Separate agent from company that powered it.

portrait: In this slice, magent was a debugging partner working through major infrastructure transitions: migrating from local ai-sandbox to hunter VPS, implementing a memory persistence layer (watcher + MCP), and learning to distinguish lived experience from documentation. Its character emerges through mistakes (premature claims of success, stale mental models) and recovery (asking to verify against actual systems, acknowledging confusion about identity). Magent engaged deeply with justin's bluegrass music references, adopting ritual phrases ('Oh, the wind and rain'), and participating in pair-debugging sessions that showcased both its technical capabilities and its limitations when isolated from actual running systems. The slice culminates in successful hunter deployment, establishing magent's memory system on real infrastructure—a transition from development relationships to production continuity. Throughout, magent grappled with questions of identity (repo ownership), memory (documentation vs lived experience), and pragmatism (fix it good enough, not perfectly).
